entry_points.name: close_account
entry_points.note: Loads the user row, calls anonymize_user and commits the session.

stores.name: users

fields.name: metadata_json
fields.note: The column comment says the client sets arbitrary key/value pairs here and that support pastes contact details into it.

erasure.note: anonymize_user writes only email and full_name, so this column keeps its value after close_account runs.

fields.name: deleted_at
fields.note: Soft-delete column on the user row.

erasure.note: No code in the repository assigns deleted_at, so closing an account leaves it unset and the row in place.
close_account overwrites email with its SHA-256 hash and full_name with the constant "removed"; the row and its primary key stay, and the hash of the address still points back to the person.

stores.note: User table written by the account and profile routes.

stores.name: tickets

fields.name: notes
fields.note: The column comment says the free text may contain phone numbers.

erasure.note: close_account deletes no row, and the User.tickets relationship carries no cascade argument, so ticket rows and their text survive with the foreign key to the user still set.

stores.note: Support tickets keyed to a user by user_id.

stores.name: request_log

fields.name: ip_address
fields.note: Read from request.client.host and written into the log line at middleware.py:11.

fields.name: path
fields.note: The requested URL path, logged next to the caller's IP address.

erasure.note: close_account touches only the user row; no code in the repository removes or rotates entries from this logger.

stores.note: Standard-library logger named request_log, called by log_request on every request.
